title: Erling Haaland's birth chart
metaDescription: Erling Haaland's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 29.0° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: the Sun and Saturn within 0.4°, identity wired to structure. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 29.0° Cancer, the third decan, 20° to 30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Cancer and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 11.1° Cancer; Venus stands at 10.0° Leo; Mars stands at 23.1° Cancer. The tradition reads a mind that absorbs before it argues from Mercury, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate from Venus, drive that moves on certainty and current from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest: the Sun sextile Saturn, 0.4° of separation. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Venus trine Pluto at 0.4°, and Jupiter trine Neptune at 1.2°, both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles: present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mercury stands apart from every major angle the day held. The tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Cancer at 23.1° is in fall (the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given); Jupiter in Gemini at 4.1° is in detriment (the planet opposite its home, working against the grain). The old table grades terrain, not talent: a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 water, 3 air, 2 fire, 1 earth by element and 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 3 mutable by mode. Water signs hold memory in the scheme, where nothing is quite finished and little is genuinely forgotten. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde (apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first).

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.5° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 23.1°.
